dependencies.description:

reader. The owner publishes book qualification as telemetry, yet H-Q-4a's
response never occurs: after 30 seconds of a non-qualifying book, adding orders

current-generation book state. Before the debounce expires, place no new order

Codex was out of quota, so the loop's audit/challenge/adjudicate was run offline
with two independent non-codex reviewer threads plus operator adjudication. Note
the independence caveat: both reviewers were Claude-family, so this is
different-model independence, NOT the cross-vendor independence codex supplies.
Every citation below was re-verified by the operator against the source.

The GREEN full gate of iteration 26 was TRUE BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. Seven steps and
287 mutations passed while a blocking regression sat in the change, because no
test covered disconnect-with-inventory or pre-snapshot evaluation, and both new
SETTLING tests inject a clean orders walk BEFORE the replacement leg is sized.
A mutation catalogue can only kill code the tests exercise.

--- D1. BLOCKING REGRESSION. FIXED 2026-08-19. ---

The recap predicate had no target > 0 guard, and target is legitimately 0:

  fundedReducer returns 0 on a nil book OR empty levels (run.go, the levels.Max
  !ok branch). SizesFor sets HasReduce unconditionally for any q != 0 while
  SizeR caps Reduce at funded (skew.go), so wanted stays TRUE and target is 0 --
  the !wanted branch never sees it. The predicate then degenerates to
  atRisk(side) > 0 and cancels ANY resting exit, including a compliant one.

Reachability, traced end to end and then reproduced in a test:
  ApplyDisconnect sets ResetBooks: !clean, so an ABNORMAL close calls
  core.Rig.ResetOnReconnect, which empties every level. The owner loop runs
  evaluate and pump after EVERY select arm including the event arm, so evaluate
  executes immediately with empty books. The recap sits deliberately ABOVE the
  !actionable guard, so its cancel leg dispatches from a book nothing may be
  placed against, and Conditions.Valid then holds the replacement until
  resnapshot. Same collapse at startup with adopted inventory, before the first
  snapshot lands.

Net pre-fix behaviour: on every abnormal disconnect while holding inventory, the
harness DELETED its own correctly-sized exit at the moment it went blind, and
could not replace it until reconnect and resnapshot. That is the exact inversion
of I1 ("no stop path may stop reducing risk") and A4, both of which this unit's
own comments cite. SizeR's doc says an unfundable reducer is "not placed"; the
change silently promoted that to "cancel the one you have".

This was a REGRESSION, not a pre-existing hazard: HEAD has zero
KindCancelConfirmPlace enqueue sites and no cancelConfirmed field at all, so the
entire branch is new. lip-732 also introduces the FIRST activation of the
cancel-confirm-place machinery in quote/queue.go, which was dead code until now.

The in-code comment asserting this "fires on genuine overshoot alone, never on a
compliant exit" was false at target = 0. It has been corrected in place.

FIX APPLIED: guard the predicate on target > 0. Given q != 0, target is 0
exactly when funded is 0 -- either the book is unreadable or capital is
exhausted -- and cancelling the exit is wrong in BOTH cases. Overshoot that
cannot yet be replaced is strictly safer than no exit at all.

TEST ADDED: TestAnAbnormalDisconnectDoesNotCancelTheCompliantExit in
gate_failure_test.go. The exit is sized at EXACTLY the quantized |q|, so the
only thing that can produce a reducing-side cancel is the target collapse; the
clean-close case is the control, and there is a pre-disconnect control assertion
so nothing is attributable to the fixture. Verified to FAIL on both abnormal
cases with the guard reverted and PASS with it restored. build, vet and every
harness package pass with the fix.

--- D2. CONFIRMED, STILL OPEN. Hand to the next round. ---

The replacement leg of the cancel-confirm-place is deterministically unbuildable
in production timing, so the designed confirm-then-place mechanism never
actually operates.

applyWriteResult on Absent calls ConfirmAbsent and sets cancelConfirmed but does
NOT touch pf.LiveOrders. restingOn never consults cancelConfirmed. The same loop
iteration then runs pump: the place leg is released, dequeues, and build calls
targetSize, where remainder = target - atRisk(side) and atRisk still counts the
just-cancelled order. remainder clamps to 0, build errors with "the side is
already carrying its aggregate target", the intents are dropped and a
WRITE_NOT_BUILDABLE SEV2 is raised. Recovery is the fallback path only: the next
complete walk clears LiveOrders and the latch, then decideSide places a fresh
KindPlace.

Cost per recap: one spurious SEV2, and the reducing side ABSENT from the book
for up to position_poll_s rather than the documented single dispatch cycle. The
in-code comment claiming build "sizes the remainder against the shrunken
aggregate" is false at dispatch time.

The two new SETTLING tests structurally step over this window: both inject the
clean walk BEFORE the replacement is sized, then assert the replacement does not
dispatch, and hand-reset the latch. No test in the suite builds the replacement
in the stale-LiveOrders window that production always occupies.

Not fixed here because the repair is a design decision, not a typo: the
defensible fix is to let restingOn discount quantity on a side where
cancelConfirmed is true (ConfirmAbsent is, after all, a complete verifying read
showing absence), but that trades against H-FAIL-3's rule of counting an order
until the exchange confirms it gone. That judgment is worth codex's independent
read rather than an operator's.

MISSING TEST for D2: a production-timing SETTLING case with NO manufactured
post-Absent walk, asserting the place leg acks at 1 contract with zero
WRITE_NOT_BUILDABLE anomalies.

--- D3. NOTED, NOT VERIFIED, LOW WEIGHT. ---

Possible recap churn when a reducer partial fill lands in the orders-then-
positions fetch window: q shrinks before LiveOrders.Remaining does, so atRisk
briefly exceeds target on a healthy at-touch exit. The reviewer conceded the
directive's "possibly-live quantity above target" arguably endorses firing here.
The operator did NOT independently verify the poller ordering claim. Treat as a
churn cost to weigh, not an established defect.

A composite involving stale Intent.Role on a released StageSecond place leg plus
enqueue deduping on Op() rather than Kind/Role was raised and marked UNVERIFIED
by the reviewer. Both mechanisms are pre-existing and untouched by this diff

dependencies.title: F5: H-FAIL-6's REST cross-check does not exist, and quarantine strands the reducer
dependencies.description:
Found by the lip-7u4 final-consumer audit. Distinct from lip-2vc, whose
acceptance ("no composed test shows a wedged feed reaching REDUCING") covers the
half that WORKS -- gate.Tick (harness/wsx/gate.go:597-629), called from
cmd/harness/run.go:1191, does reach REDUCING.

THREE FACTS, EACH INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED:

1. H-FAIL-6's cross-check is ABSENT, not deferred behind a stub. F5 requires:
   book silent >60s while socket healthy -> GET /markets/{t}/orderbook, compare
   prices AND SIZES through the full Target Size walk on both sides, including
   our own expected resting size; agree -> reset the staleness clock and KEEP
   QUOTING; disagree -> replace and quarantine.
   There is no REST orderbook fetch anywhere in the tree. Grepping "orderbook"
   across all non-test .go yields exactly one hit, a comment in core/levels.go.
   gate.go:622-624 admits it in its own anomaly text: "H-FAIL-6's full-depth
   comparison is deferred, so this reduces rather than trying to prove the book
   right."

2. THEREFORE F5 IS ONE-WAY. With no cross-check there is no "agree" branch, so a
   quiet market can never resolve back to quoting. It degrades to quarantine +
   REDUCING and stays there.

3. QUARANTINE BLOCKS NEW REDUCER PLACEMENT. cmd/harness/run.go:1300-1316: after
   the cancel branch, "if !actionable { continue }" skips o.decideSide for BOTH
   roles, commented "no PLACEMENT decision may be taken from a quarantined or
   stale book. Cancels are unaffected." Existing resting orders survive and
   cancels still work, which is how §12's "reducing: live" LOOKS satisfied.

THE HAZARD THIS COMPOSES TO, which is why it is P1 and launch-relevant:
a market goes quiet -> quarantined and REDUCING -> resnapshot is LOG-ONLY
(cmd/harness/run.go:757-782 raises RESNAPSHOT_DEFERRED SEV2 and does not
resubscribe; its own comment says the book "stays quarantined until the socket
cycles") -> so if the resting reducer is FILLED, or the position moves so the
reducer needs resizing, NO REPLACEMENT CAN BE PLACED. Inventory then sits
unmanaged until a socket cycle happens for some unrelated reason. A healthy
socket does not cycle merely because one market went silent, so on a one-market
pilot there may be nothing to cycle it.

That is a directional position held open, unattended, with no reducer and no
mechanism to place one. It is exactly the state CR-1 must not be able to reach.

SCOPE -- ADJUDICATED 2026-08-14 BY THE OPERATOR. DO NOT RE-ADJUDICATE.
The earlier (a)/(b)/(c) fork is CLOSED. The driver correctly ruled SPEC_CONFLICT
on it, the operator patched notes/harness-spec.md, and the contract now answers
the question. Implement the spec as it currently reads; see NOTES for the full
decision and the file:line starting points.

In short: new rule H-FAIL-7 retains H-FAIL-6's REST cross-check book as the
reducer's pricing source for the duration of an F5 quarantine, so the reducing
side stays live and resizable while the adding side stays off. A13 is not
weakened -- the quarantined websocket book remains a source for nothing.
H-FAIL-7 also requires an immediate in-session resubscription on disagree, so
the quarantine ends on snapshot + reconcile as F2's does instead of waiting for
a socket cycle that a one-market pilot may never get.

This means (a) and (b) are both IN SCOPE and required, and (c) is superseded by
a narrower, better-sourced rule than the one it proposed.

launch-relevant finding must.

dependencies.title: H-CLOSE-1: stop adding when the ticker leaves the active LIP programme set
dependencies.description:
cmd/harness/run.go passes quote.MarketInput.ProgramEnded=false unconditionally, with the reasoning at the call site.

H-CLOSE-1: at end_date there is no reward left to earn, so the adding quote has no purpose; the reducing quote stays and is now genuinely free.

The naive read -- program.end_date from /incentive_programs -- is WRONG. Live universe 2026-08-07: LIP programmes are short REWARD PERIODS inside a market's life. Sampled programme KXSILVER15M-26AUG071800-00 ran start_date 21:45Z -> end_date 22:00Z on a market whose close_time was 22:00Z, while 180 of 200 active programmes sit on markets closing >24h out. So end_date passing is a gap between periods, not the end of the incentive.

The correct condition is membership: this ticker is in no active programme any more. That is a poll of /incentive_programs?status=active (public, unsigned) plus a membership test, on roughly the schedule_poll_s cadence. feed.Universe cannot answer it -- it returns {ticker: target_size} and a ticker order, and go/feed is hash-pinned.

Cost of leaving it: economic, not safety. false keeps the adding quote alive, so the failure is quoting while unpaid. Every rule bounding real exposure is wired (close lead, the operator early-close backoff, inventory ladder, gate, capital caps). The opposite error is worse: reading a between-periods gap as programme-ended stops quoting in a market that is still paying.

=== 2026-08-11: DISK HEADROOM IS NOT THEORETICAL — MEASURED ===

The negative-control gate is a build-cache bomb, and it took out two consecutive
R0 gate rounds for lip-jy4 before the cause was visible.

MEASURED:
- ~/Library/Caches/go-build had grown to ~193GB. 'go clean -cache' took over ten
  minutes and returned the volume from 100% used / 1.1GB free to 55% / 194GB free.
- One full 273-mutation round consumes roughly 13GB of NEW cache entries: round 2
  started with 9.8GB free and died partway through the catalogue at ~46MB per
  mutation. Budget ~15GB free per round, and treat that as a floor.
- Go's automatic cache trimming (entries unused for 5 days) does not reclaim this
  fast enough, because every mutated tree produces cache entries that are unique
  to that mutation and are never reused.

HOW IT PRESENTED (both times as something else):
- Round 1: the baseline suite failed immediately after the 273-mutation preflight.
  Reported as an unreadable 'FAIL negative-control (rc=1)' because of lip-8k3.
- Round 2: 'shutil.Error: [Errno 28] No space left on device' inside
  make_sandbox's copytree, ~3.5h in, followed by a cascade of DID-NOT-BUILD and
  'caught, but NOT by the named test -> []' rows for mutations that had compiled
  successfully in that same run's preflight minutes earlier.

The second signature is the dangerous one: a disk-exhausted round looks exactly
like a catalogue that rotted, and an agent or operator reading only the summary
would start 'fixing' mutations that are fine.

FOR CR-1 OPERATIONS:
- q01 is a 4-6h real run that writes a durable evidence bundle, an anomaly journal
  and a SQLite store to this same volume. A full disk during q01 fails
  qualification for a reason that has nothing to do with the harness.
- The runbook needs a pre-flight free-space assertion before both a gate round and
  any live run, plus a scheduled 'go clean -cache'. Consider having gates.sh refuse
  to start below a threshold rather than discovering it at hour 3.5.

=== 2026-08-11: DISK HEADROOM IS NOT THEORETICAL — MEASURED ===

The negative-control gate is a build-cache bomb, and it took out two consecutive
R0 gate rounds for lip-jy4 before the cause was visible.

MEASURED:
- ~/Library/Caches/go-build had grown to ~193GB. 'go clean -cache' took over ten
  minutes and returned the volume from 100% used / 1.1GB free to 55% / 194GB free.
- One full 273-mutation round consumes roughly 13GB of NEW cache entries: round 2
  started with 9.8GB free and died partway through the catalogue at ~46MB per
  mutation. Budget ~15GB free per round, and treat that as a floor.
- Go's automatic cache trimming (entries unused for 5 days) does not reclaim this
  fast enough, because every mutated tree produces cache entries that are unique
  to that mutation and are never reused.

HOW IT PRESENTED (both times as something else):
- Round 1: the baseline suite failed immediately after the 273-mutation preflight.
  Reported as an unreadable 'FAIL negative-control (rc=1)' because of lip-8k3.
- Round 2: 'shutil.Error: [Errno 28] No space left on device' inside

  'caught, but NOT by the named test -> []' rows for mutations that had compiled
  successfully in that same run's preflight minutes earlier.

The second signature is the dangerous one: a disk-exhausted round looks exactly
like a catalogue that rotted, and an agent or operator reading only the summary
would start 'fixing' mutations that are fine.

this ticker present in only 17 of 61 recent snapshots was a paging artifact, not
a membership lapse.

The hazard the choice is made against is a programme lapsing ACROSS THE MANDATED
RESTART DRILL: every restart re-runs the active-programme walk, and a ticker that
has fallen out by then turns KeepAlive:true into a respawn loop against a start
refusal, with the run dead and nothing reporting it. This ticker's programme end
and market close are both 2026-09-03T14:00Z -- 22 days of runway, so neither can
fire inside a 4-6h window. Book traffic is not a qualification risk: the monitor

TWO OPERATING TRAPS recorded before the run rather than after:

  - The restart drill must SIGKILL the harness CHILD, by pid. The launchd job's
    argv is `/usr/bin/caffeinate -is <harness> ...`

dependencies.title: fee_cost is parsed with ParsePrice4; 6-decimal fees discard every fills walk and block q01
dependencies.description:
The fills walk applies the PRICE parser to `fee_cost`, and fees carry a finer
quantum than prices. Every complete fills walk on this account is therefore
discarded, the fills freshness clock never advances, and q01's portfolio
freshness bar can never be met.

MEASURED 2026-08-12 on the first real q01 attempt (candidate dc77e3f, binary
sha256 1882b82f..., ticker KXMAMDANIMENTION-26AUG12-SAFE). Three minutes in:

  monitor    observed 60  fresh 60            -- fine
  portfolio  observed 12  fresh_complete 0  incomplete_walks 12

Every single portfolio walk incomplete, one FILL_UNCONVERTIBLE anomaly per 5s
poll. q01 requires >= 99% fresh+complete portfolio slots; the run sat at 0% and
could not recover, so it was stopped rather than left to burn six hours into a
guaranteed assessment failure.

THE CHAIN

  harness/wsx/portfolio.go:564  fee4, err := rest.ParsePrice4(f.FeeCost)
  harness/rest/read.go:50       len(fracPart) > 4 -> error, "this parser will
                                not round"
  harness/wsx/portfolio.go:399  convertFills error -> FILL_UNCONVERTIBLE SEV1,
                                eff.Stop = true, whole result discarded

The offending value is real exchange data: fill 1582884a-1f64-7c20-fab4-b40468ad5df6
has fee_cost "0.017200" -- six decimals. ParsePrice4's measured quantum is 1e-4
dollars, which is right for PRICES. It is not right for fees: a fee is a
fraction of a price and is quoted finer. The defect is applying a price parser
to a fee field, not the parser's strictness.

NOT WORKAROUNDABLE OPERATIONALLY. The fill is historical and sits on the real
account, so it appears in every complete fills walk forever. There is no config
knob, no ticker change and no restart that avoids it. q01 CANNOT RUN on this
account until this is fixed.

THE PARSER BEHAVED CORRECTLY. read.go's own comment says "Truncating here would
silently discard precision the exchange chose to send. If the quantum ever gets
finer, this must surface as an error and be handled, not rounded away." That is
exactly what happened: it surfaced, loudly, through the real alert channel, on a
read-only run, before any writer existed. This is the qualification doing its
job.

FIX. Give fees their own conversion rather than widening ParsePrice4 -- prices
and fees have different measured quanta and collapsing them would lose the
assertion that makes ParsePrice4 useful. Measure the actual fee quantum from
live data before choosing the width. H-ORD-8 uses fee_cost as its INDEPENDENT
check (portfolio.go:551), so whatever type it becomes must keep that comparison
meaningful.

SEQUENCING. This forces a gate round before q01 can be attempted again, so
lip-83o (the launchd plist boolean defect) should ride along in the SAME round
rather than being worked around a second time.
dependencies.notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 by go/cmd/conform, read-only, against the real account. This settles the type question the description left open.

THE FEE QUANTUM IS 1e-6 DOLLARS, and it is not occasional. All 15 fills in account history carry fee_cost with EXACTLY six decimal places -- the decimal-place histogram is {6: 15}, with no other width present. Eight distinct values appear and ParsePrice4 refuses every one of them, INCLUDING "0.000000": the refusal is on width, not magnitude, so a zero fee is just as unconvertible as a large one. There is no subset of this account history on which the current parser succeeds, which is why every complete walk was discarded rather than most of them.

THE TARGET TYPE ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY CORRECT. wsx/portfolio.go:577 writes Fee: num.Money(fee4 * 100) with the comment "Money is 1e-6 dollars and a Price4 is 1e-4 dollars". So the destination is already a 1e-6 quantity and the code is upcasting into it -- the only wrong step is routing the string through a 1e-4 parser first. Parsing fee_cost directly into num.Money at 1e-6 removes the conversion rather than adding one, and leaves ParsePrice4 untouched so its 1e-4 assertion keeps its meaning, which the description asked for.

H-ORD-8 COMPARISON PRESERVED: portfolio.go:551 uses fee_cost as S2s independent corroborator via Fee > 0. A 1e-6 parse keeps that exact comparison and makes it sharper, since a fee below 1e-4 currently has nowhere to land.

SEVERITY IS UNDERSTATED ABOVE. The description says the freshness clock never advances and q01 cannot meet its bar. What actually happens is worse: eff.Stop reaches run.go:1315 requestStop("portfolio_read"), the global machine goes RUNNING -> WINDING_DOWN -> DRAINED, and quote/machine.go:451 states there is NO transition back to RUNNING without an operator action. Attempt 1s evidence confirms it -- global=DRAINED for 22,547 state samples starting 2.3s after launch, against 51 samples of RUNNING;QUOTING over the first 0.3s. q01 attempt 1 was not slowly failing a bar; it was permanently halted at t+2.3s and spent its remaining 3m22s drained. Everything downstream of a SUCCESSFUL portfolio walk -- adoption, quoting, rung behaviour, the H-checks, multi-hour freshness -- has therefore never executed against real data at all.

BLOCKED BY A SECOND DEFECT ON THE SAME FILLS: see lip-jhi. Eight of these fifteen fills are is_taker=true with non-zero fees, and the first thing that happens once the fee parses is TAKER_FILL -> eff.Stop -> the same durable halt. Fixing this bead alone moves the halt one layer deeper without moving it later. The two must ship together.

Added here rather than filed separately, on the driver's explicit ruling: this
bead already carries the obligation to provide a reducer for every nonzero q, and
a second bead over the same seam would be a duplicate the tracker has to
reconcile later.

WHAT WAS OBSERVED, implementing lip-gp8's loss floor. A non-flat position in ANY
market other than the configured one makes the WHOLE trading P&L permanently
unevaluable. The harness subscribes to one book, so no mark exists for a foreign
market; H-HALT-5 forbids both skipping it and inventing a price for it, so the
figure refuses with SEV2 PNL_MARK_UNAVAILABLE once per episode and pnl_kill
cannot fire at all until the account is flat in that market.

THE DRIVER'S RULING: lip-gp8 is behaving CORRECTLY and must not be changed.
Making it ignore a foreign market would convert an explicit refusal into a false
P&L, which is the failure H-HALT-5 exists to prevent. The defect is UPSTREAM:
§7.5 adopts the position while H-ORD-5b says the harness subscribes to whatever
it holds, and the current one-ticker core.Rig, gate and supervisor do not satisfy
that rule. The same foreign position therefore also lacks the reducer A4
requires -- which is this bead's subject.

SO THE VECTOR IS: a held NON-SELECTED market must be subscribed, marked and
reduced, not merely tracked. The eventual ratchet needs a compiling
M-DGG-SELECTEDONLY caught by a COMPOSED restart/adoption test proving exactly
that -- a mutation caught by its own package's tests proves internals, not
wiring (lip-7u4).

BLOCKS S=12. If the verification matrix shows dynamic managed-set subscription is
too large for this unit, split a P1 child AT THAT POINT rather than up front.
=== 2026-08-11, CR-1 OPERATING-ENVELOPE ADJUDICATION ===
The prior H-ORD-5b note made dynamic subscription, marking and reduction of a
held non-selected market part of the one-market pilot. That silently turns CR-1
into part of CR-2.

For CR-1 the dedicated account is a binding precondition: startup must refuse if
complete account truth contains a non-flat position or live order outside the
one declared ticker, and live foreign activity must durably stop adding without
cancelling an order the harness does not own. P&L remains correct to refuse an
unevaluable foreign position. Automatic subscription and management of the
non-selected market is deferred to CR-2, where selection/rotation exists.

This bead still owns the one-market A1-A14 enforcement and scenario matrix. It
does not own multi-market recovery merely because an audit found the broader
spec vector.

title: rest: Fills() walks all account history every call; backfill_h is client-side
description: harness/rest/read.go Fills() does a COMPLETE cursor walk then filters by `since` client-side. That is correct per H-PAGE-1 clause 2 (a server-side early stop on timestamp would make the walk incomplete, and only a complete walk may replace state), and it is fine for the pilot: 15 fills on the account, one market, days. It does not scale — at a 5s poll over months the walk grows without bound. Options when it matters: (a) measure whether /portfolio/fills honours min_ts and whether a bounded read still counts as complete for its window, (b) keep a durable high-water mark in harness.db and walk only until the first already-seen fill_id, treating THAT as the completeness criterion. Neither is safe to assume; both need the V1.8a treatment (measure, record, then code).
notes: Session blocker (2026-09-26): issue requires measured min_ts/window completeness or a proved durable high-water contract before changing exhaustive fills walks. Existing account has a small bounded historical sample; no authorized authenticated conformance experiment or complete timestamp-boundary/page fixture establishes current behavior. Preserve complete client-side backfill and require operator-provided/current read-only contract evidence before optimization.
